investment_summary:
Amazon grew net sales 12% to $716.9 billion in 2025, and AWS grew 20% [1]. Operating income rose to $80.0 billion [1]. Normalized income grew 7% to $65.4 billion, because reported EPS of $7.17 includes a $15.3 billion net gain [1].

Cash is the weak point. Capex of $128.3 billion cut free cash flow to $11.2 billion [1]. Yahoo Finance shows $7.7 billion, a gap we cannot reconcile from the sources available [2]. At $252.42, the reverse DCF needs 19.3% annual revenue growth for ten years [3]. That is above consensus FY2026 growth of 15.7% and the 11.7% three-year historical CAGR [1][3]. The implied return of 8.3% sits below the 12.4% WACC [3]. Consensus rates the stock Buy with a $326.34 target [3]. The case holds only if growth beats consensus and cash conversion recovers. The main risks are competition, the fixed-cost base and open legal matters [1].
key_takeaways: AWS margin should recover toward 36% as infrastructure scales, but its fall to 35.4% from 37.0% is the swing factor [1].
Cash returns will lag earnings until capex growth slows, since free cash flow was $11.2 billion against $128.3 billion of capex [1].
At $252.42 the stock needs 19.3% revenue growth for a decade to earn its cost of capital, above consensus 15.7% growth [3].
Diversified growth supports resilience, but unquantified legal and tax exposure keeps downside risk open until resolutions are disclosed [1].
business_overview:
Amazon.com, Inc., founded in 1994, is a multi-segment retailer and technology company. It sells products through online and physical stores, runs a third-party seller marketplace and fulfillment network, and provides cloud computing through Amazon Web Services (AWS) [1]. It reports three segments. In 2025 net sales rose 12% to $716.9 billion, with North America at $426.3 billion (59% of the total), International at $161.9 billion (23%) and AWS at $128.7 billion (18%) [1]. Prime membership bundles fast free shipping with video and live sports, and the company makes devices including Kindle, Echo and Ring [1]. Management says low prices and fast delivery remain central to its strategy [1].

Growth came from AWS and International, but segment profit growth varied. AWS sales grew 20%, yet operating income rose 14% to $45.6 billion, so its margin fell to 35.4% from 37.0% as technology and infrastructure spending absorbed much of the gain [1]. North America operating income rose 19% to $29.6 billion, lifting its margin to about 7.0% from 6.4% [1]. International operating income rose 25% to $4.75 billion, but foreign exchange contributed $903 million of that, so the underlying improvement was much smaller [1]. The filing does not disclose segment net income, so operating income is the segment profit measure [1].

Cash generation is the central issue for the investment case. Operating cash flow rose to $139.5 billion from $115.9 billion, but cash capex reached $128.3 billion, up from $77.7 billion, so free cash flow fell 71% to $11.2 billion [1]. Yahoo Finance reports FY2025 free cash flow at $7.7 billion, a gap we flag but cannot reconcile from the sources available [2]. Cash taxes fell to $8.3 billion under the 2025 Tax Act, which flattered operating cash flow [1]. Consensus, dated after the 10-K, expects FY2026 revenue of $829.2 billion and EPS of $12.80 [3].
market_position:
The filing does not quantify market share in any segment, so market position has to be judged from the segment mix and the rivals the company names [1]. In retail, Amazon competes with other online and physical retailers. In cloud, AWS competes with other cloud infrastructure providers. In advertising, it competes with search and media platforms. The filing also names healthcare, communications and logistics as arenas of competition [1]. It notes that AI and search technologies lower barriers to entry and make comparison shopping easier for smaller rivals [1]. This breadth gives Amazon scale across markets, but it also spreads pricing pressure across the business.

Customer concentration is not disclosed, so the filing cannot confirm whether major customers are blue-chip companies [1]. The customer base is spread across consumers, third-party sellers, advertisers, Prime members and AWS cloud customers [1]. AWS growth was driven by customer usage, partly offset by pricing changes on long-term contracts [1]. Third-party seller sales are rising, and the filing says the cost of the A-to-z Guarantee will increase with that volume [1]. Amazon employed about 1,576,000 people at year-end 2025 [1].

Market valuation gives a mixed view. The stock closed at $222.69 on the filing date, within a 52-week range of $161.38 to $258.60 [2]. The current price used for valuation is $252.42 [3]. Consensus rates the stock Buy with a mean target of $326.34 (range $230 to $405), as of 2026-11-24, after the 10-K [3]. Against the peer set, Amazon has the largest revenue base but trails Microsoft and Alphabet on margin and returns [4]. Its market position is strong in scale, while the returns on its growing capital base lag the leaders [4].
operating_results:
Net sales rose 12% to $716.9 billion from $638.0 billion [1]. Gross margin widened to 50.3% from 48.9% because cost of sales grew 9%, slower than sales [1]. Technology and infrastructure spending rose 23% and was the main cost pressure [1]. Operating income rose to $80.0 billion from $68.6 billion, and operating margin rose to 11.2% from 10.8%, even after $5.2 billion of FTC settlement and severance charges [1].

Diluted EPS rose to $7.17 from $5.53, but this includes a $15.3 billion net gain in other income, mostly from a price adjustment on the Anthropic convertible notes [1]. Normalized income rose 7% to $65.4 billion, which is the better measure of operating earnings growth [1]. First-quarter 2026 operating income guidance of $16.5 to $21.5 billion compares with $18.4 billion a year earlier [1]. Consensus expects FY2026 EPS of $12.80, down 0.2% from 90 days ago, and FY2027 EPS of $10.67, up 1.5% from 90 days ago [3].

Cash flow lags earnings. Free cash flow fell to $11.2 billion from $38.2 billion as capex rose, and the cash tax benefit flattered operating cash flow [1]. Yahoo Finance shows FY2025 free cash flow of $7.7 billion [2]. Quarterly EPS surprises after the 10-K are mixed. The quarter ending 2026-03-31 beat estimates by 68.2% and the quarter ending 2026-06-30 by 215.1%, but the quarter ending 2026-09-30 missed by 3.5%, at $1.89 against $1.96 [3]. Beats of that size should not be extrapolated until their source is checked. Trailing free cash flow was -$37.6 billion at 2026-09-30 [2].
risk_assessment:
The 10-K names three principal risks. First, intense competition could force lower prices or higher spending, since some rivals have greater resources and the filing says competition continues to intensify [1]. Second, a large fixed-cost base means demand misses can leave excess or insufficient fulfillment and data center capacity, with markdowns or impairments [1]. Third, legal, regulatory and tax proceedings have unpredictable outcomes, including FTC and state attorney general matters and an Indian tax assertion on cloud service fees [1]. The filing gives no dollar reserves for these matters [1].

Balance sheet and funding risk has grown. Total assets rose 31% to $818.0 billion, and net property and equipment reached $443.1 billion, 54% of assets [1]. Long-term debt rose to $65.6 billion from $52.6 billion, and the current ratio is 1.05 [1]. Yahoo Finance data dated after the 10-K show total debt of $271.9 billion and net cash of -$157.7 billion at 2026-09-30, up sharply from total debt of $153.0 billion at FY2025 on Yahoo's definition, with a cash runway of 3.0 years at the current burn [2]. Shares outstanding rose 1.3% in FY2025 and 1.2% in the latest quarter [2].

Financial quality screens are mostly sound. The Altman Z-score is 5.75, in the safe zone, the Beneish M-score of -2.59 gives no earnings-manipulation warning, and the Piotroski F-score is 6 of 9 [2]. The main risk is that free cash flow stays weak while capex keeps growing. The reverse DCF shows the current value needs 19.3% revenue growth for a decade [3]. The view would be wrong if growth beats that path while free cash flow recovers as the cash tax benefit fades [1][3].
competitors_analysis:
Peers were chosen by business model first and size second. Microsoft (cloud infrastructure, the closest rival to AWS), Alphabet (advertising and search, the main rival to Amazon's ad business) and Walmart (large-scale retail, the rival to North America) overlap most with Amazon's segments. Their revenue ranges from 0.4 to 0.9 times Amazon's [4]. Small marketplaces such as eBay and Coupang were excluded because their revenue is under 0.1 times Amazon's [4].

Amazon's profitability trails the two technology peers. Gross margin was 50.3%, against 68.8% for Microsoft and 59.7% for Alphabet [4]. EBITDA margin was 23.1%, against 55.2% and 44.9% [4]. ROIC was 16.8%, below Microsoft's 26.8% and Alphabet's 28.7%, and roughly level with Walmart's 17.1% [4]. Revenue growth of 12.4% was below Alphabet's 15.1% and Microsoft's 14.9%, but far above Walmart's 5.1% [4]. Amazon's gross margin, although lower than the technology peers', has risen every year since 2022 [4].

Amazon's valuation is the lowest of the four. EV/EBITDA was 15.4 in 2025, against 24.0 for Microsoft, 21.1 for Alphabet and 20.0 for Walmart [4]. Consensus forward EV/Sales is 3.6x, dated after the 10-K [3]. The peer tool reports Amazon's FCF conversion at 0.10, against 0.55 to 0.70 for peers, but those figures do not reconcile with the EBITDA and FCF inputs, which imply about 4.7% [4]. We treat that metric as unverified. The discount to peers is justified only if cash conversion does not recover.

investment_theses.thesis: AWS operating margin will recover above 36% in FY2026 as new infrastructure scales.
investment_theses.evidence: AWS net sales grew 20% to $128.7 billion, but operating margin fell to 35.4% from 37.0% as infrastructure spending rose [1].
investment_theses.signpost: AWS operating margin above 36% in the FY2026 10-K, filed around February 2027, with AWS sales growth of at least 20%.
investment_theses.invalidation: AWS margin stays below 35% in FY2026, or AWS sales growth falls below 15%.

investment_theses.thesis: Free cash flow turns clearly positive in FY2026 as operating cash flow catches up with capex.
investment_theses.evidence: Operating cash flow was $139.5 billion against $128.3 billion of cash capex, leaving free cash flow of $11.2 billion [1]. Trailing free cash flow was -$37.6 billion at 2026-09-30 [2].
investment_theses.signpost: FY2026 free cash flow above $11.2 billion on the 10-K basis, reported in the FY2026 10-K filed around February 2027.
investment_theses.invalidation: Trailing free cash flow is still negative in the FY2026 10-K, or net cash worsens beyond -$158 billion.

investment_theses.thesis: The stock earns its cost of capital only if revenue growth beats consensus for a decade.
investment_theses.evidence: The reverse DCF implies 19.3% annual revenue growth against consensus growth of 15.7% for FY2026 and 15.8% for FY2027, with an implied return of 8.3% against a 12.4% WACC [3].
investment_theses.signpost: FY2026 revenue growth at or above 15.7% reported in the FY2026 10-K, and consensus FY2027 revenue not revised down from $960.5 billion.
investment_theses.invalidation: FY2026 revenue growth below 15%, or a fall in consensus EPS estimates over the next 90 days.

investment_theses.thesis: Gross margin keeps rising despite competitive pressure, supporting profit growth.
investment_theses.evidence: Gross margin rose to 50.3% from 48.9% as cost of sales grew 9%, slower than sales [1]. EBITDA margin reached 23.1% [4].
investment_theses.signpost: Gross margin above 50% for FY2026 in the FY2026 10-K, with no new legal charge comparable to the $5.2 billion recorded in 2025.
investment_theses.invalidation: Gross margin falls below 50.3% for FY2026, or a material new legal reserve is recorded.
